_comment: Labelled set for the retrieval evaluation. Copy to retrieval-eval.json and fill in.
documentVersionId    a process document already uploaded and parsed in the target deployment
description          free text, so a failing case is identifiable without opening this file
expectedStandardKeys the standards a knowledgeable reviewer says apply. Order is IGNORED --
ranking is measured by position in the RESULT, not here.
expectedDepartment   for the wrong-department rate. Omit or null when the corpus has none.
expectedStandardVersionIds
OPTIONAL. The specific version of each expected standard that should be
selected -- normally the one in force. Drives wrongVersionRate.
Omit it when you are confident about the standard but not the version: the
metric SKIPS unlabelled cases rather than guessing, and reports n/a. That is
deliberate -- inventing a stricter expectation would either flatter or
unfairly penalise the system.
Worth labelling wherever a standard has several versions. Selecting the
right standard at the wrong version is the failure a reviewer is LEAST
likely to catch: the subject matter matches, every finding reads plausibly,
and the document has been measured against rules that are not in force.
An EMPTY expectedStandardKeys asserts that nothing should be retrieved. Include several of
these: a system that always returns its best guess scores well on recall while being unable to
say 'no standard here applies', and comparing against an unrelated policy reports every
requirement as a gap. Without negative cases that failure is invisible.
supersededCandidateRate needs NO labelling -- it reads the lifecycle already on each candidate,
so it reports meaningfully even before this set is complete.
Aim for a mix: single-standard, multi-standard, cross-department, multi-version, and not-covered.

cases.description: Hardware procurement procedure, Procurement dept — expects two standards
Change management procedure — single obvious standard
Staff expense claim form — corpus has no governing standard
